disease_label_per_paper: Serotonin toxicity precipitated by tramadol in the setting of polypharmacy
presentation_summary: 79-year-old woman with heart failure, diabetes, chronic pain, depression, hypothyroidism, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and prior non-Hodgkin lymphoma chemotherapy presented with generalized weakness and worsening bilateral tremors for more than one week.
She had been taking citalopram, trazodone, oxycodone, and other chronic medications; tramadol had been added one week before admission.
Family reported visual and auditory hallucinations, palpitations, diaphoresis, and behavior/mood change.
Initial vital signs were temperature 100.9 F, pulse 77/min, respiratory rate 19/min, blood pressure 131/62 mmHg, MAP 85 mmHg, and oxygen saturation 92% on room air.

Exam showed altered mentation, disorientation, resting and intention tremor, diaphoresis, fever, episodic tachycardia/tachypnea, labored breathing, rales, edema, and reduced sensation in the left foot.
Tramadol was discontinued and oxycodone/trazodone were held; she was alert and oriented with tremors subsided within 24 hours.
